arc_assessment: The promised descent is real and well built: 01 to 05 genuinely falls from a 720 km sheet to a 240 km sheet to a water section to an oblique to a powerhouse interior, and the 04 to 05 handoff (a 20 FT dimension floating free, then acquiring its two objects) is the best junction this page has shipped in weeks. The climb does not exist as a picture: 06 is a chart, 07 is a declared no-scale field, 08 returns INSIDE the same room as 05, so the second half is a plateau plus one jump at 09, and the shape is stated in rail text rather than drawn.
zoom_reading: Descent reads at contact-sheet size without reading a word. Climb does not. Rungs 6, 7 and 8 are all at or below the floor spatially (chart, abstract count, same room as 05), so the filmstrip reads as five steps down, three flat, one step up. The declared payoff of device A, a progress glyph whose lit rung falls and rises, was the one cheap way to state the shape where the pictures can't, and it was rendered as a plain nine-tick linear progress row instead.
bookend: The geometry is exact and that is a real achievement: same conic, same coastline vertices, Cordova's mark within a pixel or two on both (slide space ~x 730, y 1030). Four declared state changes are present: water stilled, ring phantom-dashed, circuit closed, Polaris lit. But 09 reads as a subtraction plus an unannounced paper change. The ground hue shifts from slate (#0E1A20 family) on 01 to navy on 09, the hachure gets LOUDER and lighter on 09 than on 01, and the steel network is drawn at higher contrast. A sealed close should be quieter than the cover; this one is noisier. 09 loses the copper, the index box and the sub, and gains only the Polaris, so the net felt move is 'less' rather than 'answered'.

junction_pulls.pull: The gold hairline index box around Prince William Sound on 01 (slide coords ~x 495-950, y 830-1150) is literally slide 02's frame, drawn in true projected coordinates. The reader swipes to open the box. Undercut only by the copper edge tease failing to connect.

Verbal only: 'nothing leaves' demands 'then where does it go'. There is no shared visual element across the cut except the footer rail, and the palette jumps from cold slate map to saturated mint water. Nothing in 02's picture points at 03's.
Water continues as a material: the tailrace section becomes Orca Inlet. Real, but the mint teal of 03 does not survive into 04's slate, so the 'same water' reading is broken by hue.
The 20 FT dimension floats free on 04 with nothing to measure, then on 05 the same 840 px rule acquires a cabinet at one end and a generator at the other. Best junction in the deck.
'170 kW COMPUTING' is labelled on 05 and 06's headline answers '170 against what'; the copper busbar carries through as the baseline. Clean.
'one town's numbers' to 'how many towns'. Carried entirely by the headline; 06's picture makes no promise about a population of towns.

'One got picked' to 'picked for what'. Strong as a sentence, but it is the deck's biggest density cliff (flattest slide into densest slide) placed exactly at the turn, and 08 returns to a room 07 never showed.
Gold. 08 is the only slide since 01 with the full August 11 rail and a gold money tick; 09 opens with the same rail and one gold Polaris on the cover's frame. The palette arc lands.

weakest_transition.why: It is a pure hard cut. 02 ends on a light concrete ledge over a dark map; 03 opens on a saturated mint slab that appears nowhere else in the deck. No element crosses the seam: the copper does not continue (02's copper dead-ends at a 4 px arrow under the 56 KM plate; 03's copper is a new horizontal rule at slide y 709 that enters and exits both frame edges), the ring does not reappear, and the fog and ground hue both change. The reader has to be carried by the headline alone at the exact point the deck is asking them to accept an escalation.
weakest_transition.fix: Carry one element across. Cheapest: end 02's copper at a drawn lug on the LEFT-of-Cordova coastline and start 03's copper at the same y with the same lug shape entering from the left edge, so the conductor is visibly the same conductor. Second, pull 03's water toward 04's slate (drop the mint band's OKLCH chroma to match the verdigris token #3E7A6B rather than the near-mint it renders at) so 02, 03 and 04 read as one body of water under one light.

continuity_findings.problem: The declared edge tease does not complete. 01's copper exits the RIGHT edge at slide y ~756 (visible, but a ~4 px orange stub at 432 px). 02's copper enters the TOP edge at slide x ~526 and runs down. A right-edge exit cannot be answered by a top-edge entry; the tease reads as a stray mark on 01 and a new object on 02.
continuity_findings.fix: Either bring 02's Railbelt thread in from the LEFT edge at slide y 756 to match, or drop the tease on 01 and stop claiming it.

continuity_findings.problem: State table says TURNED INWARD, a 180 degree return terminating on the server's input lug. The render shows a single near-straight conductor running from the generator LEFT across the whole frame, terminating with a floating dot at slide x ~240 in mid-air and passing into the cabinet's right face, and it ALSO exits the right frame edge at slide y ~743. That is slide 01's CUT state repeated on the hero, and the argument state for 05 is simply absent.
continuity_findings.fix: Re-render 05. Draw the return: conductor leaves the generator, drops to the floor plane, turns 180 degrees at a drawn lug and terminates ON the cabinet's input face. Do not let it cross the right frame edge; only slide 01 is allowed to do that.

continuity_findings.problem: REMOVED does not read. The server mesh was not removed; a mid-grey rectangle occupies the identical footprint (slide x 40-125, y 665-911) inside the phantom outline, so at 432 px the box is still a box. The declared thumb takeaway, 'the glowing box is gone', is false. Worse, the body copy plate's bottom edge (slide y ~665) overlaps the top of the phantom outline and the line 'conditions. (C01, C02, ...)' sits on the void, burying the slide's focal point under type.
continuity_findings.fix: Re-render 08. The volume inside the phantom outline must be FLOOR, not a grey solid, with only the dashed outline and the bare lug in it. Raise the body plate so its bottom clears slide y 640, and let the void be the emptiest area on the slide.

continuity_findings.problem: The August 11 rail occupies three different anchors on the three slides that carry it in full. Slide 01: slide-space x 628-1013, y 493-651 (mid-frame, butted with zero gutter against the Fraunces sub, and semi-transparent over the '150 KM' and '125 KM' contour labels which bleed through the plate). Slide 08: x ~730-1030, y ~327-490, wedged against the body plate. Slide 09: x 628-1013, y 84-236. The collapsed hollow tick on 02-07 sits at a fixed top-right (~x 960, y 115). So the motif's collapsed state and its expanded state live in different places, which reads as two different objects rather than one motif changing shape.
continuity_findings.fix: Pin the rail's top-left to the tick's anchor on all nine. On 01 that also clears the sub's gutter and lifts the plate off the contour labels.

continuity_findings.problem: The nine-rung ladder is present and increments correctly (transcribed: 01 lit rung 1, 02 rung 2, 03 rung 3, 04 rung 4, 05 rung 5, 06 rung 6, 07 rung 7, 08 rung 8, 09 rung 9), but it is drawn as a flat horizontal row of nine ~2 px ticks. The declared payoff, a glyph whose lit rung DESCENDS for five and CLIMBS for three, is not in the artwork. This is the one device that could have stated the shape where 06, 07 and 08 cannot draw it, and it states nothing.
continuity_findings.fix: Redraw as a stair: nine rungs whose baseline y falls monotonically 1 to 5 and rises 6 to 9, ~26 px tall overall, lit rung filled and the rest hairline. It reads at 432 px as a V and it costs one shared footer component.

continuity_findings.problem: The ladder migrates from bottom-LEFT (beside the bar scale, on all other eight slides) to bottom-RIGHT, where it collides with the counter and renders as a stray tick immediately before the numerals, reading as an apostrophe: "'08 / 09". The bottom-right of 08 is a pile-up of four overlapping black plates (money rail, $750,000 label, footnote, counter).
continuity_findings.fix: Keep the ladder bottom-left even when the rail relabels to dollars. Give the money rail the full bottom-left band and move the $750,000 end label above the rule, not beside the counter.

continuity_findings.problem: The load-bearing number is not drawn as a measurement. There are no extension lines, no 3-to-1 arrowheads spanning the gap, and no visible span between the copper's end and Cordova's mark. The '56 KM' plate sits at the copper's terminus (slide x ~445-545, y ~400-440), 280 px from the town, so the reader sees a label near a line-end rather than a dimension across a gap. The dossier's #73 dimension call did not survive to the render.
continuity_findings.fix: Draw the dimension: extension line from Cordova's mark, extension line from the nearest segment vertex, 4 px gap and 6 px overshoot, arrowheads at both ends, the plate on the span's midpoint.

continuity_findings.problem: SPLIT AND SPILLED renders as a single orange horizontal rule at slide y ~709 running edge to edge, passing BEHIND the body copy plate and emerging on both sides. It reads as a stray drafting rule, not a conductor with a terminus, and it violates the device's own rule that the copper has a defined end. The verdigris spill branch (the small teal curve at slide x ~380 dropping into the water) is 1 px and invisible at thumb.
continuity_findings.fix: Terminate the copper inside the frame at a drawn junction, and make the spilled branch hero weight down into the tailrace so the split reads as a split.

continuity_findings.problem: Same frame, different paper. 09's ground goes navy and its hachure field is brighter and busier than 01's, and the network is drawn at higher contrast, so the return reads as a different sheet rather than the cover sealed.
continuity_findings.fix: Match 09's ground and hachure alpha to 01's exactly (same seed already claimed). Let the ONLY differences be the four declared state changes.

continuity_findings.problem: The rendered legend reads '8 ROWS OF 25', which contradicts both the storyboard (10 rows of 20 at 42 px pitch, one microgrid per foot, row 840 px wide) and copy.json's authored legend string ('200 DRAWN AT 42 PX PITCH'). At 25 columns the rows span roughly the full 1080 px, so the twenty-foot lock that governs 05's dimension and 06's baseline does not hold on 07, and the deck's best geometric idea silently loses a third of its members.
continuity_findings.fix: Re-lay the field at 20 columns by 10 rows at 42 px pitch, row width 840 px aligned to 05's dimension and 06's baseline, and resync the legend string to copy.json.

rhythm_findings.problem: The breather is in exactly the right place and it works. It is the calmest slide, the quiet zone is the sky as planned, and the floating dimension does real narrative work rather than decorating. No change.

06 is not too dense after 05; the real problem is the opposite. 06 is the deck's densest slide (a 570 x 745 px black table plate in the top right, a detail circle, a big-number tile, four label plates on one row, three coloured rules stacked within 30 px of the baseline) and 07 is the deck's flattest (a low-contrast field of grey rings on dark ground, a large dead region at slide x 640-1080, y 240-660, and a long serif paragraph). The reader goes hero, slab, then nothing. Attention drops at 07 and never recovers before the turn at 08, which is then the densest slide again.
rhythm_findings.fix: Thin 06 by moving the five-row table off its opaque plate onto the lit slab band, and give 07 one bright event other than the pip: raise the emboss depth and the raking contrast on the bottom three rows as the dossier specified, which currently is not visible at all.

rhythm_findings.problem: Three dense slides land 06, 08 and the tail of 05 with only 07's slump between them, so the deck fatigues in its last third rather than escalating.
rhythm_findings.fix: Cut 08's body from 44 words to about 30 (the AURORA-AI expansion can move to the caption; the slide needs the amount, the acronym and the mechanism, not the PI title inline) and let the void carry the argument.

consistency_findings.problem: Transcribed: 01 / 09, 02 / 09, 03 / 09, 04 / 09, 05 / 09, 06 / 09, 07 / 09, 08 / 09, 09 / 09. All present, all correct, all bottom-right in the same anchor, all JetBrains Mono 26. This fixture is clean.

The mint water band is the most saturated field in the deck by a wide margin and reads as pasted from another deck against 02's and 04's slate. The declared verdigris token is #3E7A6B; what renders is materially brighter and greener.
consistency_findings.fix: Clamp the band to the declared token and hold the OKLCH chroma gate.

consistency_findings.problem: Three label plates sit on one horizontal line at slide y ~940-1010 and one of them ('20 FT') is a WHITE plate with dark type while the other two are black plates with light type. The odd plate reads as an error rather than as an emphasis.
consistency_findings.fix: Either make all three knockouts, or make the 20 FT plate gold-ruled on black so the emphasis is the deck's own gold rather than an inverted plate.

consistency_findings.problem: '1.25 MW', the third line of the HUMPBACK CREEK HYDRO label, overflows its black plate (plate bottom slide y ~1154) and lands at slide y 1168-1185 on the bare lit-slab band, immediately above the scale rail. It is the only text in the deck sitting on unmanaged ground and it visually collides with the '1 MW = 42.6 PX' rail.
consistency_findings.fix: Size the plate from the measured three-line box, or set the label as 'HUMPBACK CREEK HYDRO 1.25 MW' on two lines with a wider column.

consistency_findings.problem: The cabinet's #6EA5FF emissive strip renders near-white at 432 px, so the declared thumb takeaway ('a small glowing blue panel') fails and the two-hue thesis (copper makes, forget-me-not consumes) does not carry wordlessly on the hero. On 06 and 08 the forget-me-not is unmistakable, so 05 is the outlier.
consistency_findings.fix: Raise the emissive's chroma and lower its luminance so it reads blue rather than blown, keeping the 6 x 18 px budget.

consistency_findings.problem: Shadows hold down-and-right consistently on 05, 06, 07 and 08, and the lit-slab band recurs on 01, 02, 05, 06, 08 and 09. Physics holds. The only break is 07's Cordova pip, which carries a wide soft white bloom that no other key-lit element in the deck has.
consistency_findings.fix: Trade the bloom for a raised three-face base with a hard two-part contact shadow, which is what the dossier specified and which reads better at 432 px anyway.

thumb_pass.survives: 01's headline and the gold index box. 02's headline and the light quotation ledge. 03's headline. 04 entirely, it is the strongest thumb in the deck. 05's headline plus the copper cylinder silhouette. 06's three bars and the DETAIL A tile. 07's headline and, just, the Cordova pip. 08's three-line headline and the four partner blocks. 09's ask and the gold Polaris. All nine headlines clear 22 px equivalent and all nine counters are legible.
thumb_pass.dies: Every instance of device B except 02's thread and 06's busbar: 01's cut stub is ~4 px of orange on the right margin, 03's rule reads as a hairline, 05's conductor reads as a decorative swoosh, 09's sealed loop reads as part of the Polaris badge. Device A's ladder is ~2 px ticks and is gone entirely. The hollow gold tick on 02-07 survives as a speck but its shape change against the solid rail is not readable at 432 px. On 03 the fraction dies completely: the reader sees a teal slab, not a fifth of anything, and the two bound rules sit 10 thumb-px apart. On 08 the removal dies: the grey rectangle still reads as a server.
thumb_pass.story_lands: Partially. Reading only the thumbs in order a stranger gets: nothing leaves Cordova, the nearest line is 56 km, a fifth goes nowhere (asserted, not shown), the man's quote and a measured 20 feet, twenty feet from the turbine, the whole co-op to scale, over 200 island grids, the money is not for the data center, and one closing question. That is the argument. What is lost at thumb size is every piece of EVIDENCE the pictures were supposed to carry wordlessly: the fraction, the removal, the copper's terminus. The deck currently argues in headlines and illustrates in footnotes.

caption_check.promise_kept: Yes on all three named payloads. 'The map with no line out' is 01 and 09, 'the twenty feet drawn true' is 04 and 05, 'what the $725,000 buys' is 08. The caption's ZOOM structure mirrors the deck's own shape, which is unusually well matched.
caption_check.problem: The caption closes on 'What has to already exist in a village before AURORA-AI does anything there?' while slide 09 closes on 'If the power can't leave, who should get to use it?'. Two different questions at the same moment. The slide's question is the better one, it is debatable by any Alaskan, and it is the one the deck actually earned. The caption's question is a precondition audit that only utility engineers can answer, and a reader who has just read slide 09 has to switch questions to comment.
caption_check.fix: Make the caption's closing question the slide-09 ask verbatim, and move the precondition question into the aftercare reply the owner posts himself, where it will restart a thread that has already started.

predicted_bail_point.why: 05 pays big and 06 spends the reader's remaining attention on a table. 07 then offers the lowest contrast in the deck, a five-line serif paragraph that says exactly what its headline already said, a large dead region in its upper right, and no visual promise pointing at 08. Nothing on 07 is new except the count, and the count is in the headline, so there is no reason to stay and no hook to leave with. Secondary risk at 03: its headline is strong enough to carry the swipe, but its picture fails to show the fifth, so a reader who came for evidence starts discounting the deck there and bails one or two slides later, which is exactly 07.
predicted_bail_point.fix: Give 07 one thing 06 did not have and 08 needs: a single lit event in the bottom band. Raise the raking emboss on the last three rows so the field reads as a lit surface, give Cordova's pip a hard three-face base and contact shadow instead of the bloom, and cut the body from 26 words to about 14 so the eye reaches the field faster. Then plant 08's void: put one phantom-dashed rectangle at the same slide coordinates on 07 as the removed server occupies on 08, so the swipe has a shape to complete.

ranked_fixes.fix: Re-render. Actually remove the server volume (slide x 40-125, y 665-911) so the void is floor, and raise the body plate so its bottom clears slide y 640. Worth the cost without argument: this is THE TURN, the deck's whole thesis is 'take the server away and the software still reaches in', and right now the server is still there under a paragraph.

Re-render. Make the unused fraction read as a fraction: draw the full flow column with a visible top and bottom, tint only 20 to 25 percent of it verdigris, put the two bound rules where the reader can see them bracket something, and clamp the mint to the declared token. Worth the cost: 03 is the escalation and it is currently an assertion with a decorative slab under it.

Re-render. Bring the generator fully inside the frame, terminate the copper on the cabinet's input lug via the declared 180 degree return, stop it crossing the right edge, and fix the emissive to read blue. Worth the cost: this is the hero, and its copper currently repeats slide 01's state, which breaks the device's one rule.

Re-render. Draw the 56 km as a real dimension call spanning the copper's lug to Cordova's mark, and bring the conductor in from the LEFT edge at slide y 756 to complete 01's tease. Worth the cost: the deck's second slide carries its load-bearing number and does not draw it.

All nine: redraw device A's ladder as a descending-then-climbing stair, and pin device C's rail to one anchor (the tick's top-right position) on 01, 08 and 09. These are shared footer/header components, so they are one change applied nine times, and together they deliver the two declared payoffs the render is currently missing.

Re-lay the field at 20 x 10 on a 840 px row so the twenty-foot lock holds, resync the legend to copy.json, raise the bottom-row emboss, cut the body to about 14 words, and plant 08's void shape. This is the bail point; it is worth a re-render.
Fix the '1.25 MW' plate overflow at slide y 1168-1185 and unstack the three coloured rules at the baseline. Can ride along with any other re-render pass.
Match 09's ground hue and hachure alpha to 01's so the bookend returns rather than repapers. Ride-along.
Unpile the bottom-right corner: ladder back to bottom-left, $750,000 label above the rule, footnote on its own line, so the counter stops rendering as "'08 / 09". Ride-along.
Caption: replace the closing question with slide 09's ask verbatim and demote the precondition question to the owner's own first reply.
